conditions: The message must be posted in the channel #deploys.
The message's author must be Priya Sharma.
The message must have been posted on September 23 (taken as the most recent September 23, i.e. 2026-09-23, absent other context).
The message must be about a/the rollback (its content concerns a rollback).
The target is a specific channel message (top-level, not a reply buried in a thread unless that's how the channel surfaces it) to which a :thumbsup: emoji reaction should be attached.
Exactly one such message should exist/be identifiable as 'the' message matching all the above.

readings: September 23 of the current year (2026), since no year is given and that's the most recent occurrence
September 23 of some other year, if there's prior shared context (e.g., a past incident) not visible from the request alone
A message whose text explicitly discusses or mentions a rollback
Any message related to a rollback event even if it doesn't use the word 'rollback' (e.g., 'reverting the deploy')
A top-level message posted directly in the #deploys channel
A message posted by Priya in a thread within #deploys (still 'in' the channel, just nested)

turn2.differences: The conditions match the request closely. r6 (uniqueness) is a check on the whole set rather than a per-message property; it holds since exactly one message (000002) satisfies r1-r4. r5's thread-vs-top-level caveat is moot here since the data model has no threading field, so every message is a top-level channel post.

ambiguity_effects.explain: With today given as 2026-09-26, the only sensible referent is the most recent September 23 (2026-09-23); a careful reader would not hesitate, and the dataset only contains 2026 dates anyway.
Whether this requires the literal word rollback or just substantive content about one does not matter here, since every rollback-related candidate message uses the word explicitly.
Whether a thread reply counts as posted in the channel is a real general question, but this dataset has no thread structure, so it never affects the outcome.

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing reads like an ordinary Slack request: naming the channel, the poster's full name, a date, and a topic to disambiguate is how a colleague or workspace bot would naturally ask for this. Nothing suggests test scaffolding.
